import pandas as pd

# Load the capital dataset again
capital_df = pd.read_csv('/data/capital.csv')

# Drop non-numeric columns
capital_df = capital_df.drop(columns=['group', 'color'])

# Replace commas with periods and convert to numeric
capital_df = capital_df.apply(lambda x: x.str.replace(',', '.').astype(float) if x.dtype == 'O' else x)

# Perform PCA on the forms of capital
pca = PCA(n_components=1)
capital_pca = pca.fit_transform(capital_df)

# Add the PC1 values to the capital dataframe
capital_df['PC1'] = capital_pca

# Display the first few rows of the updated dataframe
capital_df.head()

# Filter the data for the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) periods
middle_neolithic = capital_df[(capital_df['BCE'] >= 3000) & (capital_df['BCE'] <= 3400)]
younger_neolithic = capital_df[(capital_df['BCE'] >= 2300) & (capital_df['BCE'] <= 2900)]

# Calculate the mean PC1 values for the Middle Neolithic and Younger Neolithic periods
middle_neolithic_mean_pc1 = middle_neolithic['PC1'].mean()
younger_neolithic_mean_pc1 = younger_neolithic['PC1'].mean()

middle_neolithic_mean_pc1, younger_neolithic_mean_pc1

from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

# Perform a t-test to compare the mean PC1 values of the two periods
t_statistic, p_value = ttest_ind(middle_neolithic['PC1'], younger_neolithic['PC1'])

t_statistic, p_value
